title: NA capacity thresholds + escalation — talking track (scratch)
content:
Subject: Internal update for NA capacity thresholds and escalation (talk tracks + Q&A) — DRAFT

TL;DR:
- We are updating the way we enforce regional capacity thresholds for North America to reduce cross-customer interference during peak hours. This is a configuration & policy change (no infra rollout required).
- Goal: protect latency SLOs for high-tier customers and reduce tail latency for hosted API users while keeping degradation predictable.
- What teams need to know: GtM (customer comms), Ops/SRE (escalation & monitoring), Support (customer-facing responses), and Eng (tuning & exceptions).

Audience:
- Managers briefing their teams before all-hands
- Customer-facing leads prepping post-incident comms and usage queries
- On-call SRE/ops for next 2 weeks (watch window)

Purpose of this doc:
- Provide short, consistent talking points for small team syncs and manager updates
- Surface anticipated Q&A and suggested wording for Support and Account teams
- Log TODOs and follow-ups (numbers, docs, PRs)

Key messages (one-liners for managers):
1) We’re introducing regional capacity thresholds in NA to keep latency predictable for paying customers; this is proactive, not a reaction.
2) Most customers will see no change; a small subset of high-throughput users may see rate-limits or graceful fallbacks during extreme peaks.
3) We’re monitoring closely and will roll back or relax policies where there are clear regressions tied to customer impact.

Expanded talking points (for team leads):
- Why: unexpected spike patterns plus a few noisy tenants caused tail latency regressions at 95th/99th percentiles last month. Thresholds let us isolate noisy flows without wholesale throttling.
- How it works (high-level): we set soft thresholds per-region that influence routing & per-tenant burst budgets. When a threshold approaches, traffic will be routed to compatible model-variant fallbacks or subject to brief, rolling soft-throttles.
- Who it affects: Hosted API customers on free/standard tiers and any low-priority background batch jobs. Dedicated customers and reserved pools are unaffected unless explicitly configured.
- Timeline: config change scheduled for NA on 11/12 (weekend) with increased monitoring through 11/26.
- Escalation: if a customer reports production impact, open JIRA INF-4821 and ping #ops-escalations; SRE lead on-call will evaluate and escalate to eng infra.

Suggested manager script (30s):
"Heads up — we’ll enable regional capacity thresholds in North America this weekend to protect latency SLOs. Most of our customers won’t notice any change; for a few high-throughput tenants we may apply short, controlled fallbacks so other customers aren’t impacted. Reach out to Support or #ops-escalations if you see anything unexpected — we’ll revert or tune quickly."

Support & Account FAQ (short answers):
Q: Will my customers get throttled?
A: In most cases no. Only a small subset of extremely bursty traffic patterns will be affected with soft throttles or fallback to a compatible model variant; we prefer predictable fallbacks over unpredictable latency spikes.

Q: Does this affect Dedicated customers?
A: No — reserved/dedicated pools are isolated. If a Dedicated customer reports impact, escalate immediately; that’s an exception path and we’ll treat it with highest priority.

Q: Will I be billed differently?
A: No immediate billing changes. If we need to recommend changes to model variants or capacity, we’ll coordinate account teams ahead of any cost-impacting changes.

Q: What if a customer wants the old behavior?
A: We can evaluate per-account exceptions (requires an engineering review and a temporary override). Open INF-4821 with details (customer, traffic pattern, sample request IDs).

Anticipated follow-up questions (internal):
- Exact thresholds numbers? (TODO — get SRE/infra confirmation; currently using percentile-based config: soft limit at 92nd, hard at 99.5th.)
- Are fallbacks always to lower-cost variants? (No — we pick compatible functional variants that preserve behavior; sometimes they’re more expensive but we prefer lower latency.)
- How long will overrides take? (~1–3 business hours once filled in JIRA + on-call acceptance)

Monitoring & alerts (ops notes):
- Primary dashboards: INF-NA-latency-95/99, INF-region-evictions, INF-tenant-burst-budget.
- Pager rules: if region 99p latency > target for 5m and eviction-rate > X, page on-call SRE.
- Post-change watch: 72-hour high-frequency sampling + daily review for 2 weeks.

Customer comms snippets (use for outbound messages or support templates):
- Short (for support): "We rolled out a regional protection policy to keep latency steady during high load. We've routed some of your traffic to a compatible fallback to preserve request reliability — this should be transparent. If you see degraded functionality, please send sample request IDs."
- Longer (for account): "To ensure consistent performance across our platform, we implemented a regional capacity policy that prioritizes steady latency for production requests. Most customers won't notice any change; if you'd like us to review your workload and provide guidance, we're happy to schedule a technical review."

All-hands talking bullets (1–2 min):
- "This week we turned on regional capacity thresholds in NA to protect customer-facing latency. It’s a conservative measure to keep our SLAs predictable as traffic grows. We’ll monitor closely and keep teams updated. Thanks to SRE and infra for the fast turnaround."

Open items / TODOs (owner initials):
- Finalize exact threshold numbers and publish to Confluence (S.P. / SRE) [due 11/10]
- Add update to public status page if any customer-visible incidents occur (Support)
- Create a short KB article for Support with sample troubleshooting steps and log locations (M.C.)
- Confirm weekend on-call coverage and runbook (Ops)

Notes to self (scratch):
- Confirm whether we should proactively email top-10 highest-throughput accounts or wait for inbound questions. Leaning toward proactive note for top 3 only.
- Possible follow-on: suggest a traffic-smoothing rate limiter for noisy tenants (longer term).

References / links (internal):
- Confluence: NA capacity changes (linked above)
- JIRA: INF-4821 (policy + rollback playbook)
- Slack: #ops-escalations thread (linked above)

— end of draft —

Notes: still rough, want manager concise bullets + support templates finalized. Keep this in users/ for iteration.
